title: Tongue-tie release
what: The doctor makes a small cut in the short band under the tongue. After that the tongue moves more freely.
why: When a short band makes it hard for a baby to breastfeed or for a child to say certain sounds.
duration: the procedure usually takes a few minutes, up to 30 minutes in older children
tell_doctor: How your baby feeds at the breast or bottle
Which sounds are hard for your child
Blood or clotting disorders, bleeding in relatives

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A baby is usually fed after the procedure. Ask the clinic when to feed before it.

prepare.title: Mood
prepare.text: Calmly explain to an older child that the doctor will help the tongue move more freely.

bring: A referral from a speech therapist or pediatrician, if you have one
steps: The doctor examines the tongue and the band
Numbing is given, as a gel or an injection
The band is cut with scissors or a laser
The small wound is pressed with a gauze
feel: A baby usually cries only briefly
A little blood, which usually stops quickly
The area under the tongue is sore for a few days
after: A baby is usually put to the breast right away
For older children: soft, cool food for 1 to 2 days
A white patch will appear under the tongue. This is how it heals
Tongue exercises as the doctor or speech therapist shows you
red_flags: Bleeding does not stop after 10 to 15 minutes of pressure
Your child refuses to eat and drink

faq.q: Does it have to be done?
faq.a: Not always. The doctor decides if the band gets in the way of eating or speaking.

faq.q: Will my child speak correctly right away?
faq.a: Not right away. Speech therapy sessions are often needed.

reminders.text: Tongue-tie release tomorrow. Ask the clinic when to feed your child before the procedure.
